From it you can talk, praise, insult, joke, give, trade, court, propose, recruit, and read why they feel as they do about you.

Standings are per party member. An NPC has an opinion of each of your characters, and only the member doing the talking moves it. The panel lists every member's standing.

A free chat field takes typed input and generates a reply. With the local language model enabled in experimental options it writes the reply; otherwise a Markov chain does.

peopleOpinion.title: How Somebody Decides What They Think of You
peopleOpinion.description:
An NPC's opinion of one of your characters is built from four parts:

- base opinion, moved by everything you have done to them: kindness, insults, gifts, trades, known crimes
- trait compatibility, applied before a word is spoken
- ideology, how close your creeds sit on the five axes, worth up to a dozen points either way
- hygiene, how the two of you smell to each other right now (see the hygiene page)

Gaining standing also feeds the social need of the character who gained it.

Attraction is tracked separately from opinion. Conversation, gifts and trade move opinion only; courting moves attraction. It starts at zero, and a romantic move reads trait compatibility and hygiene a second time at a heavier weight.

peopleLives.title: People Have Lives
peopleLives.description:
Everyone's life advances whenever time does: minute by minute, and through any time skip, sleeping, waiting or travelling.

- they are born somewhere on a date and keep a record of every move since, with reasons
- they meet, date, marry, divorce and separate, preferring partners from their own settlement
- they hold careers from the real job list, with a job history from their first working year, changes as they age, and retirement
- dishonest ones carry criminal histories: convictions, sentences served or being served off screen, outstanding bounties, and a standing that recovers slowly once debts are paid
- a conviction can cost someone their job

A year spent in cryogenic sleep is a year in which everyone aged, changed jobs, married and buried each other.

peopleTalking.title: What People Say to Each Other
peopleTalking.description:
Two people who wander close together stop, face each other and hold a conversation, one line at a time in thought bubbles. The tone, positive, negative, neutral or a debate, comes from what they think of each other and from their personalities. Finishing one moves both opinions and is recorded as having met.

People sharing a room while busy trade two line exchanges without stopping.

Each of the twenty five personalities has its own lines for weather and time of day, its own inner monologue, and its own openers and closers.

The last twenty conversations of every person can be read in their panel.

peopleSettlements.title: Settlements and What Happens To Them
peopleSettlements.description:
Every settlement carries three civic meters:

- prosperity: employment, the national economy, recent events
- security: crime per head, the honesty of the local captain of the guard, national stability, and how wanted you are
- mood: built from the other two plus national unrest, festivals, epidemics and street traffic

Episodes sit on top of the meters:

- crime wave: starts when security collapses. Crime pays better and the crackdown catches more thieves, so the wave breaks itself
- boom and bust: start at the extremes of prosperity and swing hiring, crime, divorce, shop prices and market sentiment, then erode their own cause
- festival: declared by a thriving town. Mood and bustle up, shops fuller, pickpockets working the crowds
- epidemic: rare, and worse in miserable towns. Mood, hiring and shop traffic collapse and hygiene drains fast until it burns out

Transitions feed the news, the stock market, hiring, crime rates, theft difficulty, national politics and gossip. Unemployment feeds crime, crime feeds crackdowns, crackdowns feed prisons, prisons feed unemployment.

peoplePolitics.title: Politics
peoplePolitics.description:
Every hyperpower has a government, and their shapes differ: theocracies, single party states, parliamentary monarchies, technocracies, sultanates, divine pantheons, serene republics, corporatocracies, warband confederacies. Each has parties, orders or clans, a political class with charisma, integrity, cunning and ambition, a head of state, and meters for legitimacy, stability, unrest, economy and treasury.

Elections run in each power's own idiom: general elections, papal conclaves over several ballots, politburo plenums announcing 99% results, wealth weighted shareholder meetings, goblin moots where the runner up risks being eaten, divine ascension tournaments, palace successions, and the Archive's Great Examination. Results are recorded permanently.

Between elections: scandals, edicts, protests, riots, coups, revolutions, assassinations, referendums, festivals, rumours spreading through the population, and rulers ageing and dying.

Every person has a political identity: five axis ideology, a party, an engagement level from apathetic through voter and activist to organizer, a voting record, and grudges against the parties that beat theirs.

Each settlement elects a mayor from its own population every year. The mayor appoints a captain of the guard, a tax collector and a high priest from among their ideological allies.

peopleFactions.title: Factions and Reputation
peopleFactions.description:
Eighteen factions. Standing with each runs from -100 to +100, moved by contracts taken, crimes committed, adventures resolved and sides taken.

Factions answer to hyperpowers. A faction with a hyperpower is a branch of it, so credit earned with a parent can carry its branches.

Standing decides what work is offered, what prices are quoted, who will speak to you, and which seats you may take.

peopleONU.title: The Assembly
peopleONU.description:
Every hyperpower holds a seat on neutral ground inside the Omega Tower. Once a game week the delegations argue about alliances, trade, war and recent events.

A party member can take a seat. The seat, the standing it earns and the weekly stipend are that character's alone, and the stipend scales with their standing with the power they serve. A member whose standing falls far enough is dismissed.

Only powers that already think neutrally or well of that character will take them. Joining raises their standing with the power and every branch under it. A character joins once; resigning costs far more than joining paid.

A session rolls one to three motions. Two to five delegations take the floor, each in its own voice, you answer, and then every seat votes. Ballots are public, turning each named tile green or red as it is read, or secret, shuffling them unlabelled and turning them at once so only the tally is certain.

Grave motions, war, admission, territory, artifacts, theonuclear devices and the goblin question, go to the Security Council: the five strongest powers left standing by your century, measured on military, economic, population, information and arcane strength. They approve or veto, majority carries, and the Secretary General breaks a tie. Without one, the motion fails.

The Tourists hold a chair with no ballot, take the floor when they like, and admit nobody.

lawCrime.title: Crime and Bounty
lawCrime.description:
Every crime is filed by name with its own bounty value. Your bounty is the sum of them.

Deliberate crimes: theft, breaking and entering, vehicle theft, and others. Accidental ones too, such as running someone over.

Bounty lowers the security meter of settlements you are in, becomes gossip, changes how the guard behaves, and is read out in court.

The crime record can be viewed at any time and settled through the police portal.

lawPolice.title: The Police Portal
lawPolice.description:
The N€police application on the Hypernet is the continental police portal, and it settles your record without waiting to be caught.

- case file: every charge with its fine. Charges can be settled one at a time or all at once, which removes them from the record and lowers the bounty
- self-report: confess something not yet registered. A self filed charge is entered at half the usual fine, and raises the bounty until settled or served
- custody: turn yourself in, which puts you in a cell where the bounty is ground down by time served, or request a hearing before Eris

Both custody options leave the computer, because the cells and the courtroom are places on the map.

lawTrial.title: The Trial
lawTrial.description:
Justice is administered by Eris, and a trial is generated rather than scripted. The courtroom, gallery, staff and ambience are rolled fresh each time, she cites invented case law and produces invented exhibits mid hearing, and lines resolve their alternatives as they are spoken.

Counsel is retained before the hearing opens. Three options: hire one of five advocates, nominate a party member, or stand alone. The five are people from your world, fixed for its lifetime, with their rank written onto their profile: level, INT, WIS, Law specialization and job. Recruiting one into your party strikes them off the bar and the next name in the queue replaces them.

The brief shows each option's sprite, level, INT, WIS, Law level, opinion of you, fee, and the projected odds of every outcome, computed with the model the verdict runs on. The odds swing on Eris's mood. She greets counsel in her own voice and, in some moods, throws them out, which loses their bonus and does not refund the fee.

Representing yourself, or having a companion stand up, earns a few points of the Law specialization per hearing, and that level feeds back into the odds. A professional teaches the party nothing.

The hearing is a plea, guilty or not guilty, then a series of choices, then a verdict that depends heavily on her mood.

Evenings spent with Eris raise a bond, and a defendant she has dined with meets a warmer mood wheel, a lower conviction chance, shorter sentences, and at high enough bond a dismissal before the charges are read. Some evenings buy nothing, and she says so.

Sandbox mode has a reverse trial, where you play Eris and judge someone else.

lawPrison.title: Sentences and Prison
lawPrison.description:
Sentences come in two shapes.

- a named term is served by the game clock. Time passes in the cells and the bounty is cleared on release
- an open ended sentence has no release date and grinds the bounty down day by day until nothing is left

Turning yourself in at the police portal goes straight to the second kind without a hearing.

On release, Eris comments, according to how the two of you stand.

lawEris.title: Dating Eris
lawEris.description:
Eris can be courted. An evening with her is a generated scene.

It happens in a biome, and each biome owns its opening, its questions, its romantic beat, its chaotic beat, its shared activity and its local incidents. A scenario is rolled on top, picnic, seance, stakeout and others, so one biome hosts many evenings.

Her mood is rolled from sixteen: playful, romantic, chaotic, nervous, confident, caring, guilty, crazed, psyched out, high on solipsism, eldritch, melancholy, smug, paranoid, prophetic, bored. It can shift mid date, changing her voice and her heartbeat. In the eldritch mood her lines warp, her pulse reads things that are not numbers, and the portrait misbehaves.

Each date also rolls a register, sincere, capricious or completely bonkers, which scales how often the evening is interrupted and how hard her feelings swing. She interrupts with dares, up to robbing a bank.

Your own answers are generated too: any choice list can grow weird, awkward, chaotic or blunt wildcard answers, and how she takes one is a roll of her mood.

Two heartbeats are drawn on screen, yours and hers, and both move with the evening. She remembers past dates and brings them up. She keeps a separate relationship score for every party member, benched ones included, and sometimes turns towards one of your companions mid date.

The first date that ends well pays a blade seed, once per save.

Dates feed into the courtroom (see the trial page).

societyMail.title: The Post
societyMail.description:
A party can write to another party in the same world, or to a party in a different world on your machine. The letter waits in their mailbox until someone plays them.

A letter carries a delivery date on the recipient world's clock, and the sender can hold it back by days, months or years. Until that date passes, the letter is in transit and does not show. Writing to your own party with a delay is a letter to your future self.

Money and goods can be enclosed. They leave the sender's pockets at once and are handed over when the recipient collects them.

Post inside one world is free. Crossing to another world is priced on the two commodities that survive the crossing, oil and souls: their prices multiplied, doubled once per step of dimensional distance, never less than three hundred thousand euros. In practice tens of millions, and billions between distant dimensions.

societyNews.title: The News
societyNews.description:
The world writes its own news, and items carry effects: property prices, shop occupancy, market sentiment.

Settlement episodes, riots, coups, elections, epidemics and the mayor's divorce all become headlines. The real estate market moves on them, the stock market takes sentiment from them, and people talk about them.

societyDiary.title: The Party Diary
societyDiary.description:
The diary is the record one party keeps of its own life, written as it happens.

It records: journeys and arrivals with the hour, planet landings, bridge warps, first entry into a named place, going down into a structure, dungeon floor changes, sleeping, waiting, cryogenic sleep and the year it woke in, fights won and what was in them, bosses felled, fleeing, losing, arena streaks, people joining and leaving, deaths, retirements and recalls, levels, pets, creatures talked round, births, pregnancies, friendships and enmities, courtships, evenings with Eris, deaths of people you knew, diseases caught and recovered from, limbs lost, augments fitted, field surgery, notable finds, artifacts, purchases and sales, thefts, property, loans, share trades, crimes, charges, trials, verdicts, prison, shifts worked, crops sown and reaped, things forged, cooked, brewed and built, skills learned, technologies researched, quests, bestiary entries, minigames played, television watched and dreams had.

Not recorded: ordinary conversation, statue descriptions, states coming and going, and discarded items.

Entries are stored as keys, so a diary written in one language reads correctly in another.

The banter system takes the newest lines and turns them into what the party talks about.

societyTopics.title: Conversation Topics
societyTopics.description:
Some dialogue teaches a topic, written in square brackets in the line where it appears. Once one character hears it, the whole party knows it.

A dialogue option that requires a topic is invisible until someone in the party knows it, not greyed out.

Every topic learned is announced. The Topics tab of this book lists them with who knows each one. Some topics have a page of their own, which appears once the topic is learned.

societyArmy.title: Armies
societyArmy.description:
Beyond the party of three there is an army. Troops are recruited by faction, up to a hundred, and the count is drawn over your sprite on the world map.

Other armies fill the world map. About a fifth are faction armies of two hundred to a thousand troops, which stay inside their own country's borders, at least three per country. The rest are independent bands of five to thirty drawn from several factions, which roam anywhere and spawn near you. They move when you move.

Touching one starts a field battle in a real time tactical view: your units in yellow, theirs in red, formed up by role, close quarters in front, support behind, ranged at the back, fighting on their own stats. Wounded troops drop to one hit point and stop fighting; killed troops are gone for good. The wheel zooms and dragging pans.

societyMultiplayer.title: Multiplayer
societyMultiplayer.description:
Two ways to play with other people.

Online, through a central server or through Steam. A server session supports many players, of whom the nearest eight are drawn on one map, party members first. A Steam lobby caps at eight and sets rich presence, so friends see Join Game in their friends list.

Local split screen, two players on one machine with a gamepad each. The viewports are independent and merge into one when the players are close. Player two interacts with events and triggers things directly.

Split screen also runs a hot seat for minigames without a split screen session on the overworld. Real time arcade carts let either player steer; chess, pool and bowling alternate turns.

During a map battle the viewports merge, player two's avatar becomes the second party member's battler, and they drive the command menu on their own character's turn.

societyHistory.title: The Century Behind You
societyHistory.description:
Before you take a step, the world has lived through a century: a generated alternate history of Europe from 1900 to 2001.

It produces coups, elections, purges and assassinations; wars, sieges, mutinies and conquests; fifty kinds of paranormal anomaly, occult rites and the Squishing itself; scientific expeditions, natural disasters and organised crime; economic shifts and technological breakthroughs. The weighting favours the paranormal and the occult.

That history sets which hyperpowers exist and how strong they are, which five sit on the Security Council, what epidemics the last century saw, and what the people you meet lived through.

The full timeline is readable in the Historical Archive. The Lore tab of this book carries the chronicle of what has happened since, newest first.

econMoney.title: Money
econMoney.description:
Money is euros. Prices are written with two decimal places.

There is no separate currency except at the arcade, where euros buy tokens and tokens sell back, at a fixed rate, either at the converter machine or at the Token Exchange on the Hypernet.

The Assets screen adds cash in hand, bank balance, property, shares and livestock, less debts, and reports the result as net worth.

econShops.title: Shops
econShops.description:
Shops come in several kinds.

- counter shop: a grid of goods with categories, sorted by price, with a full detail card for anything you point at
- delivery order: arrives in one to seven days depending on price, up to six orders at once, collected later
- random daily shop: stock seeded from its own coordinates and the world seed, rerolled every in game day
- vending machine: stocked the same way. A 4x4 grid of products with codes, three purchases per slot per day, at least one odd item per machine, and one machine in ten selling nothing but odd items
- teaching shop: sells skills instead of goods, at a discount

Tax is charged on everything except skills, at a rate that moves with the economy and never drops below thirty percent.

A shop cleaned out restocks at midnight.

econStealing.title: Stealing
econStealing.description:
Anything on a shop's shelves can be stolen. The steal window scans the map for shop events and lists what they hold, with a success percentage per item computed from your agility, the item's value and its weight: light and cheap is easy, heavy and precious is not.

Ordinary shops are scanned across the whole map. A random daily merchant is scanned only within five tiles.

Getting caught files a crime under your name and lowers the settlement's security meter. During a crime wave, stealing is measurably harder.

econBank.title: Banking and Loans
econBank.description:
The bank takes deposits, pays interest on the balance, and lends money at interest against a due date.

Interest and loan maturity run on the world clock, so they accrue while you walk, sleep, travel or sit in cryogenic sleep.

Missing the due date is penalised. The Assets screen shows the balance, the outstanding loan and the due date.

econStocks.title: The Stock Market
econStocks.description:
The market trades two commodities: oil and soul crystals. A single page terminal buys and sells shares for money.

Prices are a random walk tilted by what happens in the world: settlement booms and busts, news events, the state of the powers.

The Assets screen draws the live oil and soul price graph over your portfolio. The oil price is also what the fuel pump charges and what a letter to another dimension costs.

econProperty.title: Real Estate
econProperty.description:
Thirty properties across the towns, rated one to five stars. One to three stars are cheap; a one star place costs under a thousand euros. Four and five star places are estates.

Two ways to hold one:

- buy it outright. You can then offer it for rent to NPCs, collected at midnight and on the first of the month
- rent it as a tenant. A recurring monthly cost, no subletting, and missed payments evict you and return the property to the market

Prices move with news events tied to specific towns.

Renting an inn room is separate: a room is booked for 24 game hours and cannot be double booked.

econShopOwning.title: Owning a Shop
econShopOwning.description:
A shop you own holds stock, a warehouse and a production line. Items with recipes can be produced from materials on the premises, deliveries are made at delivery points on the maps, and NPC staff can be hired to do the work.

The management screen has four pages: overview, shelf stock, warehouse, and the catalogue of what can be produced. Choosing a slot on the stock page opens the catalogue to pick what that slot makes.

econWork.title: Work
econWork.description:
More than thirty jobs across several categories. Any party member can be sent to work.

Each job states its stat requirements before you start. A member short of them is flagged but never blocked.

A shift takes game time, the screen darkens, and the outcome is generated from the worker's stats and luck. Pay is money; a disaster can cost money, deal damage, or leave a status effect.

The Job Offers menu lists what is available now and where, with duration and hourly pay.

econQuests.title: Quests
econQuests.description:
Quests are generated. A quest board's offers are derived from where the board stands.

Every quest is a list of steps. A simple quest has one; a chain has two or three, in order or in any order. The steps are detection primitives wired into the rest of the game:

- reach a set of world coordinates, or a named destination
- open an auto placed chest, or dig a site, which needs a shovel
- land on a planet and open its sample cache
- kill a specific high level enemy, force spawned at a tile, which stays there until killed even if the quest fails
- scan statues or signposts at a site
- dismantle a number of trees, rocks or piles of rubble
- open the quest board of another town
- interview a citizen of a destination through the Empathize panel
- hand over items at claim time
- wait for goods to arrive
- win arena fights, defeat a number of enemies, or hold a number of oil shares

Terms are generated with the offer and shown before you accept: reward, upfront cost, advance paid, deadline, failure penalty, breach bounty and reputation change.

Scams lie about them.

Rewards and difficulty scale on the party's median level. The board's second tab lists signed contracts with progress and countdowns, and lets you collect or abandon, which triggers the failure clauses.

The quest log is a board of sticky notes in three columns, to do, in progress and done, draggable between columns.

econNotices.title: Reading a Notice
econNotices.description:
A quest notice is written in the voice of whoever pinned it up. Dozens of faction registers and a couple of dozen personality registers exist: a corporate contract, a goblin scrawl, a redacted military bill, a nervous private plea.

What is left out, what is over explained and what is plainly a lie are readable before you accept. The terms panel gives the numbers.

econVending.title: Arcade Tokens
econVending.description:
Arcade machines take tokens. Tokens are bought with euros at the converter machine or at the Token Exchange on the Hypernet, and unused tokens can be cashed back in.

Both quote the same rate.

craftThinker.title: The Workbench
craftThinker.description:
The Thinker is the general workbench: assembling and dismantling.

The recipe is written on the item itself. Assembling consumes the listed materials; dismantling salvages an item back into pieces.

A recipe stays hidden until it has been made once. Common recipes are on the board from the start.

Base crafting materials come from dismantling the world: felling trees, mining rocks, breaking furniture, salvaging gear.

craftForge.title: The Forge
craftForge.description:
Every weapon and armour in the game is on the forge board from your first visit. Training changes which of them you can make.

Four tabs: what you can smith now, what you could make but lack materials for (with how many lines of the bill are short), what is above your training (with the tier it waits for), and what this party has already forged.

About thirty one trades are in play, one per item: a robe is Tailoring, a wig is Wig Making, a costume is Cosplay, a ring is Jewelry Making, a rifle is Gunsmithing, a circuit woven coat is Electronics.

Each finished piece is registered as its own entry with its own identity, so two never stack. Three things set its sheet: how far past the required tier the smith's trade is trained, how rich the bill that went into the crucible was, and the heat on the day. Every parameter then drifts on its own and the price follows.

Finishes are offered as a strip of swatches. The seed the 3D model is turned under is rolled once, shown in the preview, and kept on the piece.

Smelt melts a carried piece back into materials: half the bill, more from a well made piece.

The party switcher decides which tab an entry falls into, whether the forge button lights, and who earns the specialization points.

craftAlchemy.title: Alchemistry
craftAlchemy.description:
Every alchemical recipe is readable from the start and nothing is gated behind a class.

A recipe is copied onto a bench, and the bench is what you edit and run, so one recipe can be set up two ways at once.

Success is a skill check. Each recipe demands a set of specializations at a minimum tier.

- meeting every requirement: 0% failure
- each tier short of any requirement raises the failure chance
- tiers above what the recipe asks pay out as extra product, one more flask per couple of surplus tiers, up to a cap

Step durations are game minutes, so a batch cooks while you walk, work, travel or sleep, and finishes when the clock says.

A bench set to repeat rebuys its reagents and starts again on finishing, and stands down with a warning when the pack cannot pay for a run.

craftCooking.title: Cooking
craftCooking.description:
Cooking combines two recovery items into one. The first item's recovery is doubled and the second's is added, so order matters.

Cooking two of the same thing adds a random adjective instead, carrying a bonus or a penalty. The result's name is built from the first word of the first ingredient and the last word of the second.

Food carries calories, fat and protein, and a cooked meal is worth what went into it.

craftBrewing.title: Brewing
craftBrewing.description:
Barrels ferment on the world clock. Load a barrel, leave it, and brewing and distilling proceed while you play.

It is the slowest crafting and needs no attention.

craftFurniture.title: Building and Furniture
craftFurniture.description:
The Build menu places furniture on tiles, snapped to the grid. Pieces can be crafted from materials, bought, and dismantled to recover materials. Multi tile pieces are supported and some can be flipped.

Placement rules: wall furniture goes on walls only, the upper tiles of ordinary furniture may overlap a wall but the lower tiles may not, and some terrain refuses furniture.

The Build menu is also where animals are bought: pick one and click a tile to place it.

craftPlants.title: Farming
craftPlants.description:
Any tilled soil can be farmed. Plants have a lifecycle driven by the clock, the season and the weather.

- plants grow only in their own seasons. Out of season they are dormant and no time accumulates
- rain speeds growth by 30%, storms by 10%, snow halves it
- a greenhouse map runs at full speed all year and multiplies growth further
- a plant at 100% is harvested on the spot when you interact with it. The management menu only opens on a plot still growing

Tilled soil on procedural maps is farmable too. The first visit to a world square rolls, from the world seed, which contiguous patches are already sown and with what, so a whole field grows the same crop.

craftAnimals.title: Animals
craftAnimals.description:
Animals are bought in the Build menu and placed on a tile. They are managed from the Assets screen, where each is a livestock asset to collect from, sell, or turn into a pet.

They grow from baby to adult over a set number of days on the world clock, and adults produce at intervals. Produce is what a living animal gives: an egg, a pail of milk, a fleece.

Every animal carries a company value paid into the party's social need when you interact with it: the leader in full, everyone else at half, once per game day per animal. Dogs, donkeys and roosters produce nothing and are kept for this.

An animal stays at the coordinate it was placed at.

craftApiary.title: Beekeeping
craftApiary.description:
A hive is a colony simulation.

Castes: queen, workers, nurses, guards, foragers and drones, each with a lifecycle from egg through larva and pupa to adult and death. The comb is drawn as hexagons, and the colony produces honey, pollen, royal jelly and wax.

Seasons and weather act on it, disease and pests threaten it, and the colony has moods and efficiency that follow how it is kept.

craftArtifacts.title: Procedural Artifacts
craftArtifacts.description:
Artifacts are generated items, weapons and armour with rolled properties. They appear in loot, in vaults, at the end of adventures, and from certain rites.

One rite turns a party member into a weapon.

craftLoot.title: How Loot Is Rolled
craftLoot.description:
Random loot is scored from 0 to 100: the party's median level plus a difficulty modifier carried by the place itself.

The score picks the rarity band:

- 0 to 20: almost everything common
- 25 to 45: common and uncommon
- 50: a balanced spread
- 75: more epic and legendary
- 100: almost everything legendary

Rarity is read off price, and the same ladder colours item names in the backpack, the shop, the reward popup and the container list.

A patron's vault pushes the tables toward the expensive end.

craftContainers.title: Containers
craftContainers.description:
Containers hold items without limit, and each is unique to its map and event. Contents are generated from the categories the container declares, weighted by rarity.

The extradimensional container can be opened from anywhere and travels with the party, as do the holds of the camper and the car.

galaxyOverview.title: The Star Map
galaxyOverview.description:
The star map is a real time 3D view of the universe at several scales: the system you are in, the galaxy, the local group, the supercluster, the cosmic web and the observable universe.

At system scale one unit is one astronomical unit, and bodies are drawn larger than life to stay visible.

Drag to orbit, wheel to zoom, arrows or stick to nudge the view. Clicking a body selects it and opens a panel naming it and offering what you can do: travel there, or land.

Planets have day and night terminators tracking their own star, independently turning cloud layers, atmospheres and rings. Star surfaces boil.

galaxyTravel.title: Travelling Between Stars
galaxyTravel.description:
Select a system and travel to it. The journey takes time and burns fuel, and fuel sets your range.

Only an ordinary fusing star can power a refuel. Main sequence stars of every class work; remnants, brown dwarfs and black holes do not. The Refuel command handles it:

- parked at a fusing star: starts the pumps
- fusing star elsewhere in the system: plots the short hop
- otherwise: plots a course to the nearest system with one

The pumps engage on arrival.

On any map inside the ship, the view through the windows shows where you actually are, the planet you orbit or the star you are parked at, and it streaks and scrolls while under way.

galaxyShip.title: Your Starship
galaxyShip.description:
The ship is generated. Hull, layout, plating, panel lines, livery, decals, lit windows and wear are built procedurally, and the default appearance comes from your world's seed.

From the vehicle menu you can reroll the whole appearance or step through individual traits and keep the rest. Choices are stored; anything unchosen stays derived from the seed.

Under way the crew tends one need at a time: a meal, a wash, a conversation, a game, a shift of sleep. Eating consumes food from the hold, and an empty hold sends them to do something else.

galaxyLanding.title: Landing
galaxyLanding.description:
In orbit you can land. Where landing sites exist you pick from a list; otherwise you touch down on the surface.

An alien surface is an explorable map, generated like Earth's but from a different palette. Dozens of alien biomes exist, chosen by the type of world you landed on.

- encounters are not scaled to your party or to your distance from home. The planet's own level decides, rolled per planet and readable from its biosignature before you commit
- there is nothing to forage. Food comes from butchering local wildlife
- a body stripped of its resources stays stripped

Finds are written into the diary, and identified species go into the bestiary's alien page.

galaxyAnomalies.title: Anomalies
galaxyAnomalies.description:
Every star system with planets carries at least one anomalous world, marked with a question mark.

Holding orbit over it offers to investigate, once only. What follows is a branching encounter written for that kind of world: every choice leads somewhere and the last node pays out, in a relic, in salvage, in a fight with something native, or in nothing.

It runs the same engine as the adventures on Earth's map: combinatorial prose, a companion commenting in their own voice, and some choices offered only to a leader of the right temperament.

galaxyBodies.title: What Is Out There
galaxyBodies.description:
Stars come in the real classes and in a couple of dozen exotic kinds, each with its own model: remnants, brown dwarfs, feeding X-ray binaries and others. Systems can be binary or hold several stars, and each star is travelled to individually.

Black holes come in three weights, the largest drawn as lensed billboards with an accretion stream that coils across the whole separation.

Rogue planets drift between the stars with no sun.

About twenty real nebulae are placed at their real galactic coordinates and hand shaped: the Horsehead, the Orion Nebula, the dark nebulae and others.

Dyson spheres exist.

Above the galaxy the map continues: local group, superclusters, cosmic web filaments and the shells of the observable universe.

Our own solar system is hand authored, with its twelve real bodies, its belts and a shell of orbital debris.

galaxyPatrons.title: Patron Worlds
galaxyPatrons.description:
Some worlds in other galaxies are named after the people who paid for the game. They are habitable and life bearing, they orbit exotic objects, they sit in nine planet systems where no two planets share a type, and they are listed in the star map catalogue under Patrons.

Each of those people also owns a hatch on exactly one world map square. It cannot be dismantled and nothing grows over it. Going down opens their vault: a great hall with strongrooms and a deep back chamber, filled with money and weapons, holding every chest the template allows. The loot tables there are weighted to the expensive end.

Hatch locations are encrypted in the game data, keyed on the coordinates themselves.

galaxySky.title: The Night Sky
galaxySky.description:
A night sky chart, separate from the star map: a draggable, zoomable planisphere with stars sized by magnitude, constellations traced in gold, a right ascension and declination grid, and a Milky Way band.

Tab switches between constellation sets, European and Chinese, which trace different figures over the same stars.

Confirm recentres and fits the whole sky on screen.

hypernetOS.title: The Hypernet Desktop
hypernetOS.description:
The Hypernet is a simulated operating system of the period: desktop, taskbar, start menu, draggable and resizable windows, and a set of applications.

It has a virtual file system and registry, both saved inside your savegame, so written files and changed settings persist.

Controls:

- WASD or arrows move the focus ring between elements
- Tab and Shift Tab cycle through them
- Enter or Space activates the focused element
- Escape leaves a text field, then closes the window, then exits
- on a controller: d-pad navigates, A activates, B closes or exits, the left stick is a free cursor

hypernetBrowser.title: App: Hypernet Explorer
hypernetBrowser.description:
The browser. Tabs with their own history, back, forward, stop, refresh and home, an address bar with autocomplete, a links bar, an explorer bar with search, favorites and history, find on page, view source, saving a page into the file system, downloads, print preview and page setup, zoom, text size, encoding, a pop up blocker, mail and news, synchronize, connection status, options, help, tip of the day, about, and a 404 gateway page that suggests alternatives.

Every page in the archive is a full document. Preferences, favorites, history and downloads live in the registry and are kept in your savegame.

hypernetMyComputer.title: App: My Computer
hypernetMyComputer.description:
The file explorer. It browses the virtual file system: drives, folders, My Documents, and everything you or an application has written.

Files open in whichever application owns them: a text file in Notepad, a saved web page in the browser.

hypernetNotepad.title: App: Notepad
hypernetNotepad.description: A plain text editor writing into the virtual file system. Notes typed here are saved in your savegame, can be reopened, and can be read by any application that reads files.

hypernetControlPanel.title: App: Control Panel
hypernetControlPanel.description:
Machine settings. Your party's statistics are presented as hardware specifications. Wallpapers, display settings and the rest of the configuration live here.

Changes are stored in the registry.

hypernetTVGuide.title: App: TV Guide
hypernetTVGuide.description:
The television listings, read from the broadcast database. Browse every channel, its cast and its programmes.

Selecting a programme plays its broadcast inline, a line every couple of seconds, without leaving the desktop.

The schedule regenerates every in game week and is fixed for that week. The script is rerolled on every tune in.

hypernetObjectIndex.title: App: The Object Index
hypernetObjectIndex.description:
The archive's catalogue of every object known to exist: about eleven hundred dossiers, one per item, with all declared metadata.

The left page is the catalogue, grouped by category, with a search box. The right page is the dossier: identification, lore paragraph, commerce, physical properties, provisioning values, composition and raw declaration tags.

The lore paragraph is combinatorial and resolved from the world seed. Randomize rerolls it for this window only; it never changes the item's description elsewhere, and closing the app forgets it.

hypernetNeuroPolice.title: App: N€police
hypernetNeuroPolice.description:
The continental police portal, for settling your criminal record without waiting to be caught. Three pages:

- case file: every charge with its fine, settleable one at a time or all at once. Settling clears the charge and lowers the bounty
- self-report: confess something not yet registered. Half the usual fine, and a charge until settled or served
- custody: turn yourself in, or request a hearing before Eris

The custody options close the computer, because the cells and the courtroom are places on the map.

hypernetEurodemics.title: App: Eurodemics
hypernetEurodemics.description:
The public terminal of the continental epidemic observatory, reading the live outbreak ledger. Three pages:

- situation: outbreaks running, people currently ill, people dead, towns affected, worst hit towns, and a readout of where you are standing, including whether anyone in the party has caught something
- outbreaks: every outbreak burning, each with its daily curve, one point per day, redrawn when the model advances at midnight, over the town by town table
- archive: outbreaks this world has closed, plus the epidemics and mass hysterias of the last century

The graph plots people currently ill and people dead so far on one axis, since both are counts of people.

hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.title: App: Artifact Analyzer
hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.description: Analyses procedural artifacts and reports what they actually do.

hypernetTokenExchange.title: App: Token Exchange
hypernetTokenExchange.description: Converts euros into arcade tokens and back, at the same rate as the physical converter machine.

hypernetPhone.title: The Hexphone
hypernetPhone.description:
The party carries a mobile phone: credit, contacts, call history, an inbox of messages and a couple of built in games.

Calling a contact triggers what that person does when called. Incoming calls arrive with an answer or decline prompt.

Controls: keypad digits dial and act as shortcuts, arrows navigate lists, Enter is the menu button (select, call, open), Escape is end (back, and from the home screen it closes the phone), backspace deletes a digit while dialling.

Payphones share the same contacts and credit ledger. A payphone only places outgoing calls: no inbox, no games, no incoming calls, no saving contacts.

hypernetTV.title: Television
hypernetTV.description:
A television can be watched wherever you find one. Tuning to a channel puts you in that channel's studio room, where the programme's cast performs the broadcast. Named cast members turn to face you, take their own sprite and read their lines. A programme with no cast is narrated.

Dialogue is generated from templates over lore banks and splices in the live state of your world: the history channel and the news desk read back the simulated century and the current news. Every line picks its own wording as it is spoken.

The weekly schedule regenerates every in game week and is fixed for that week. The script is rerolled on every tune in, ten to sixteen exchanges per slot. OK advances, Cancel interrupts.

Commercial breaks sell either a product, quoted at its real price from the item database, or a political position paid for by one of the powers.

Finishing a transmission raises the Fun need of the whole party; interrupting one pays less. Anyone with the Technophobe trait loses the same amount instead.

The channel guide is drawn as a forty by twenty five teletext page.

hypernetRadio.title: The Radio
hypernetRadio.description:
Radios tune across AM, FM and EM bands. The stations are built from the music files the game ships with, so every track is somewhere on the dial.

Left and right change frequency, up and down change band, page up and page down scan for the next station, Enter marks a favourite, Shift with left and right jumps between favourites, Shift with up and down sets the volume. Between stations there is static.

The last station tuned is remembered.

hypernetMusic.title: Music and Sound
hypernetMusic.description:
Battle music is chosen in Options. A Random entry draws a different track at the start of every fight, custom tracks included, and None fights in silence.

Map music is seeded: one track per combination of biome, nation and time of day, drawn from wide pools.

Some music is generated live by a procedural music system.

Whatever plays announces itself, as a notification or as a drawn cassette, with track and artist.

Footsteps change with the surface underfoot.

gamesOverview.title: Diversions
gamesOverview.description:
The 3D games are simulations rendered through a retro shader, and most are played where you stand: the pool table, the basketball court, the bowling alley and the chess board are dropped into the scenery of the map you are on.

Playing anything feeds the Fun need of the whole party.

Control hints are not printed. The keys are the ones you already use.

Two players can share almost all of them. With a second gamepad, or the numpad on a shared keyboard, real time games let either player steer and turn based games become hot seat, with or without a split screen session.

gamesArcade.title: The Arcade Cabinet
gamesArcade.description:
Arcade cabinets take tokens, bought with euros at the converter or on the Hypernet. A cabinet keeps high scores with letter entry and runs a demo when idle.

Each cart is a complete game, drawn in colour ASCII:

- Snake, against a red computer snake competing for the same apples, with a speed doubling power up
- Manpac, a pellet maze with three hunters and power pills that make them edible
- Frogger, across roads and rivers to five home slots
- Space Invaders, with destructible barriers
- Asteroids, with splitting rocks and a wrapping screen
- Breakout, with falling capsules that widen the paddle, slow the ball or grant a life
- Centipede, winding down a mushroom patch, splitting when shot in the middle, with a spider that eats the mushrooms
- Bubble Pop, colours that stick and clusters that fall
- Boot sequence, a cabinet booting up: ROM check, RAM test, sound chip, video, security, and then a space to walk around in

gamesBowling.title: Bowling
gamesBowling.description:
A 3D alley with rigid body pin physics, simulated in metres at bowling dimensions: 18.29 metres to the head pin, a 1.07 metre lane, gutters, a 6.35 kilogram ball and 1.53 kilogram pins.

The view is the bowler's own. The camera rides the ball down the lane and cuts to the pin deck for the strike, and a pinsetter rake sweeps deadwood between rolls.

Aim, power and spin use the oscillating slider shared with pool and basketball: stop each bar where you want it.

gamesPool.title: Pool
gamesPool.description:
A nine foot table simulated in metres. Balls roll under cloth friction, throw each other off on impact, rattle in the jaws of a pocket and drop.

Aim, power and spin are set with the oscillating slider. The table is dropped into whatever scenery you are standing in.

gamesBasketball.title: Basketball
gamesBasketball.description:
A free throw shootout against a computer opponent on a half court measured in metres: a 4.57 metre free throw line, a rim 3.05 metres up with a 22.9 centimetre radius, and a backboard.

The ball arcs under gravity, clatters off the rim, banks off the backboard and drops through the net, or misses.

gamesChess.title: Chess
gamesChess.description:
Full rules chess on a low poly 3D board. Every piece is a creature from the game's 3D battler system, dealt from the world seed, so one world always fields the same two armies: a bright one for White and a dark one for Black.

Two modes: normal chess and Chaos.

gamesFishing.title: Fishing
gamesFishing.description:
First person fishing. Fish, junk and hostile encounters are built by the same procedural battler system the battles use, so a Megalodon hooked in the lake is the Megalodon you then fight.

Aim by looking around. A ring on the water shows where the cast lands, then it is a contest between the line and whatever took it.

What is in the water is what lives there.

gamesSurfing.title: Surfing
gamesSurfing.description:
First person surfing. Every wave is a travelling swell with a tilted crest, so it peels: the breaking point races along the beach at about ten metres a second and the whitewater eats the wave behind it.

You stand on the board, which pitches, rolls and slaps across the chop under the physics.

The game is reading the peel and staying ahead of it.

gamesShooting.title: The Shooting Range
gamesShooting.description:
A first person target range. The weapon in frame is the same 3D model the battle overlay raises, built, posed, aimed and fired by the weapon system, so every gun and bow handles as it does in a fight.

Nothing is equipped on your character: the range lends you the weapon and takes it back at the door, so it is also where a weapon can be tried before it is bought.

The rack holds only bows, projectile weapons and firearms.

gamesHorseRace.title: The Horse Race
gamesHorseRace.description:
A turf course in 3D: mown grass, running rails, a starting gate, distance poles, a winning post and a grandstand.

The runners are procedural creatures built from their own names: the name is hashed and handed to the battler system, which keys a coat, a colour and a build to it, so a named horse is the same horse in every world.

Odds are computed by simulating the race many times over the same step function the race then runs.

gamesTournament.title: The Monster Tournament
gamesTournament.description:
A single elimination monster tournament to bet on. Pick a fighter, place a bet in tokens, and only the fights involving your monster are shown.

The fights are run by the battle engine between two creatures: the AI picks skills, pays costs, rolls to hit, evade and crit, applies damage formulas, inflicts states, raises buffs and ticks poison at end of turn. The result is then replayed in a 3D arena with animations.

Betting does not affect the outcome.

gamesGambling.title: Slots, Scratch Cards and Tarot
gamesGambling.description:
Slot machine: a cabinet whose reels are drums. Each symbol is a plate on a facet of a cylinder, so a spin turns the drum and a landing overruns its stop and springs back. The symbols come from the game's icon set, and each one's average colour becomes its pip in the payout table.

Scratch cards: printed tickets rubbed panel by panel in any order, and the card can be turned in the light while you do it. The counter is a carousel of four products that turn on the spot.

Tarot table: the deck riffles, the reader cuts it, the cards fly to their positions face down and turn one at a time.

gamesPiano.title: The Piano
gamesPiano.description:
A playable three octave keyboard, C3 to B5. It is played with the typing keyboard laid out as two manuals, whites on one row and blacks on the row above, with a gamepad, or with the mouse. Keys light as they sound and show the button bound to them.

Playing it feeds the Fun need.

gamesLockpick.title: Lockpicking
gamesLockpick.description:
Picking a lock is a game of tetris: a falling block must fit into a partly completed puzzle. The lock's difficulty sets how hard the fit is.

It consumes a lockpick on failure. A skeleton key skips the game and opens the lock outright.

Lockpicking opens locked doors and parked cars. Being caught at it is a crime.

gamesHyperTamer.title: HyperTamer
gamesHyperTamer.description:
A virtual pet on a monochrome LCD handset. The pet is drawn from the game's creature database and has a personality that changes how it behaves.

It runs on real time: it eats, sleeps, plays and can die of neglect, and time passes while the game is closed. Training minigames raise its stats and it grows accordingly.

gamesCards.title: The Card Game
gamesCards.description:
A collectible card game with a collection, a deck builder and duels.

A card is a monster, a weapon or a piece of armour from the game's database, printed with five stats, STR, WIS, DEX, PSI and CON, each from 0 to 13. Those numbers are percentiles against that card's own roster, not raw parameters. Equipment is bolted onto a monster already on the board and its values are added, clamped to 13.

A deck is 9 to 20 cards and may only hold copies you own. Several decks can be kept and one is active. A player who never opens the deck builder is dealt the best legal deck their collection allows.

A duel is three by three. On your turn you either draw three cards or place one: a monster onto a free tile, or gear onto one of your own monsters, one weapon and one armour each. The table is dressed in the monsters' walking sprites.

When the last tile is taken, every monster looks at its four orthogonal neighbours, picks the weakest enemy among them and fights it. Every pairing is scored against one frozen snapshot of the board and all deaths land together. Most stats won takes the fight; an equal count destroys both. Whoever has more monsters standing wins, ties broken on the summed stats of the survivors.

Booster packs hold six cards from one pool, weighted so the last is never common.

Cards are also won by capturing a creature in battle. Capture picks the weakest creature still standing: mostly a question of how badly hurt it is, helped by the caster's PSI against the creature's own, and impossible against anything more than ten levels above your median. Success adds the card and kills the creature, so the corpse and the spoils still drop.

oily.description: It raises fire damage taken 899%. It lasts 5 turns.
